intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over its 1,500-year history. Then walk to the nearby Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) to admire its stunning six minarets and intricate Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide for deeper historical context.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Market Food & Shopping Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, then head to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delights, saffron, dried fruits, and local spices. Engage with vendors, taste free samples, and pick up authentic souvenirs. A guided food tour here adds rich storytelling about Ottoman trade history.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in a local kitchen where you'll learn to prepare classic Turkish dishes such as meze, börek, lamb kebabs, and baklava. Classes typically include a visit to a local market to source fresh ingredients, followed by a communal meal with your instructor. A deeply immersive cultural and culinary experience.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Treasury, view sacred relics, and take a guided tour of the Harem — the private royal quarters — to uncover the fascinating and complex world of Ottoman court life. The palace gardens also offer sweeping views of the Bosphorus.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise with Street Food Evening
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden boat for a scenic Bosphorus cruise at sunset, passing by Ottoman-era palaces, waterfront mansions (yalıs), and the iconic bridges connecting Europe and Asia. After docking, explore the Karaköy waterfront for a street food evening — try balık ekmek (fish sandwiches), simit, and fresh mussels stuffed with spiced rice from local vendors.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit from airport to Aegean Bliss Resort. Take the affordable Havaist airport bus or metro to save on transport costs (approx. 30-50 TRY vs. 400+ TRY for a taxi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, freshen up, and take a leisurely walk along the nearby waterfront/beachfront area to get oriented. Explore the immediate neighborhood, find a local bakkal (corner store) for snacks and essentials.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearest local bazaar street or neighborhood market for a gentle first evening stroll. Visit a simple lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) near the hotel for your first authentic Istanbul meal.

meals.breakfast: Grab a simit (sesame bread ring) and tea from a street vendor near the airport or hotel — under 20 TRY
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick börek (savory pastry) from a local pastane (pastry shop) near the hotel — under 40 TRY
meals.dinner: Lokanta-style meal: lentil soup, bread, and a main dish like kuru fasulye (white bean stew) at a neighborhood eatery — under 100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light. Get your Istanbul transport card (İstanbulkart) from any metro station — it saves significant money on all public transport. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport but compare rates at city exchange offices for better deals.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — now a mosque, free entry for non-prayer times. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat crowds. Marvel at the Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and layered history spanning 1,500 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Blue Mosque (Sultanahmet Camii) — free entry. Explore the Hippodrome of Constantinople (At Meydanı), the ancient obelisks, and the surrounding Sultanahmet Square. Visit the underground Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — modest entry fee (~150 TRY).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Sultanahmet neighborhood as it lights up at dusk. Visit a rooftop tea house for çay (Turkish tea) with views of the illuminated mosques.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the hotel or a nearby kahvaltı salonu — tea, olives, cheese, eggs, tomatoes — under 80 TRY
meals.lunch: Kumpir (stuffed baked potato) from a street vendor in Sultanahmet or a simple pide (Turkish flatbread) restaurant — under 80 TRY
meals.dinner: Traditional soup and kebab at a local Sultanahmet lokanta away from the main tourist strip — under 120 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Sultanahmet is Istanbul's historic heart. Wear modest clothing for mosque visits (shoulders and knees covered). Shoes must be removed inside mosques. Avoid tourist trap restaurants directly on the square — walk one block further for better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Topkapi Palace (Topkapı Sarayı) — the opulent seat of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years. Entry fee (~350 TRY) is well worth it. See the Imperial Treasury, Harem (separate ticket ~200 TRY), and stunning Bosphorus views from the terraces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through Gülhane Park (free, beautiful in May with blooming flowers) to the waterfront. Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex (~100 TRY) — one of the world's great ancient collections, often overlooked by tourists.
day_by_day.evening: Take a ferry from Eminönü pier across to Kadıköy on the Asian side (İstanbulkart fare ~15 TRY). Explore Kadıköy's vibrant market streets and local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Simit with cream cheese and tea from a street cart near the hotel — under 30 TRY
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a local market or grab a döner wrap near Topkapi — under 70 TRY
meals.dinner: Explore Kadıköy's food scene: fresh fish sandwich (balık ekmek) or a full meal at a meyhane (tavern) — under 150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Buy Topkapi tickets online in advance if possible to avoid queues. The Harem is highly recommended — don't skip it. The ferry ride itself is a wonderful experience with panoramic city views.

day_by_day.morning: Dive into the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with 4,000+ shops. Free entry. Browse carpets, ceramics, spices, and jewelry. Practice your bargaining skills — initial prices are often 3x the fair value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes downhill to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) near Eminönü. Buy local spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and nuts at much better prices than tourist shops. Explore the surrounding Eminönü waterfront area.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Galata Bridge fishermen at sunset. Walk across the bridge to Karaköy neighborhood. Explore the hip, artsy streets of Karaköy and Galata area.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at a local kahvaltı spot near the hotel — under 80 TRY
meals.lunch: Balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from the famous boats moored at Eminönü waterfront — under 60 TRY. Add a cup of fresh pomegranate juice (~30 TRY).
meals.dinner: Mezes and grilled fish at a simple Karaköy restaurant — under 150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: In the Grand Bazaar, don't feel pressured to buy. Shopkeepers will offer tea — accepting is fine and doesn't obligate a purchase. The best buys are Turkish tea sets, spices, and hand-painted ceramics. Avoid 'authentic' carpet shops with aggressive salespeople.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably Istanbul's most beautiful mosque, built by Mimar Sinan in 1557. Free entry. Explore the surrounding Süleymaniye neighborhood with its historic medrese (theological school) buildings and quiet courtyards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through the Fatih neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most traditional and authentic districts. Visit the Fatih Mosque and explore the weekly Fatih street market (if running). See everyday Istanbul life far from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Beyoğlu district. Walk up İstiklal Avenue (İstiklal Caddesi) — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard — from Tünel to Taksim Square. Browse the shops, street musicians, and art galleries.

meals.breakfast: Menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local esnaf lokantası (workers' restaurant) — under 60 TRY
meals.lunch: Kuru fasulye and rice at a traditional Fatih lokanta — a classic Turkish comfort meal under 80 TRY
meals.dinner: Lahmacun (thin Turkish pizza) and ayran at an İstiklal side-street restaurant — under 100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Süleymaniye Mosque is often quieter than the Blue Mosque and arguably more architecturally impressive. The Fatih neighborhood is very conservative — dress modestly. İstiklal Avenue is best explored in the evening when it comes alive.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public ferry (İstanbulkart) for a Bosphorus experience — ride the commuter ferry from Eminönü to Anadolu Kavağı (the last stop on the Asian side). This 90-minute scenic journey passes palaces, fortresses, and mansions at a fraction of the tourist cruise cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Anadolu Kavağı village at the mouth of the Bosphorus. Hike up to the medieval Yoros Castle ruins for panoramic views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. The hike takes about 30 minutes each way.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry back to Eminönü. Stop at Karaköy for a fresh simit and tea while watching the city lights reflect on the water.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the hotel or a quick stop at a local pastane before catching the ferry — under 60 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at one of the simple waterfront restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı village — under 150 TRY (this is a splurge day for lunch)
meals.dinner: Simple soup and pide at a neighborhood lokanta near the hotel — under 100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry is one of Istanbul's greatest budget travel secrets — you get the full scenic experience for just the standard transit fare. Check ferry schedules in advance on the İDO or Şehir Hatları apps. The Anadolu Kavağı ferry runs limited daily departures.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace on the European Bosphorus shore. Guided tours only (~400 TRY). The opulent interiors with massive chandeliers and gold-leaf ceilings are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Beşiktaş waterfront promenade. Explore the Beşiktaş neighborhood — a lively, authentic district beloved by locals. Visit the Çırağan Palace exterior (now a hotel) and the scenic Yıldız Park (free entry) above.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Beşiktaş's evening street food scene around the fish market (balık pazarı). This is a local favorite area away from tourist pricing.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local bakery stop — under 80 TRY
meals.lunch: Kokoreç sandwich (seasoned lamb intestines — adventurous but delicious!) from a Beşiktaş street stall — under 60 TRY
meals.dinner: Fresh fish and meze at a Beşiktaş balık evi (fish house) — under 180 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe tickets sell out — book online in advance. Photography is not allowed inside the palace. Yıldız Park is beautiful in May with blooming gardens and is completely free — a great afternoon escape.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side via ferry to Üsküdar. Visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque and the hilltop Çamlıca Mosque — Istanbul's largest, with panoramic city views. Take a local bus or taxi up to Büyük Çamlıca Hill for the best city panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Üsküdar's traditional neighborhood streets. Visit the Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) — the iconic tower in the Bosphorus. You can view it from the waterfront for free or take a boat out to it (~100 TRY).
day_by_day.evening: Return to European side. Visit Ortaköy neighborhood — famous for its beautiful waterfront mosque and vibrant evening atmosphere. Try the famous Ortaköy kumpir (loaded baked potato).

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast at an Üsküdar kahvaltı café with Bosphorus views — under 100 TRY
meals.lunch: Gözleme (savory stuffed flatbread) from a street vendor in Üsküdar — under 60 TRY
meals.dinner: Kumpir loaded with toppings at Ortaköy's famous kumpir stalls — under 80 TRY. Add a waffle for dessert (~50 TRY).

day_by_day.notes: Üsküdar has a very traditional, authentic atmosphere quite different from the European side. The Asian side generally has lower prices. Ortaköy is best visited in the evening — it gets very lively with locals and is great for people-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii/Museum) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — housing some of the world's finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes. Entry fee (~100 TRY). The surrounding neighborhood has some of Istanbul's best-preserved old city walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the ancient Theodosian Walls (land walls) — 5th-century Byzantine fortifications stretching across the city. These UNESCO-listed walls are largely free to explore. Visit the Yedikule Fortress (Yedi Kule) for a modest entry fee (~50 TRY).
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Istanbul. Visit the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — colorful, historic Greek and Jewish quarters with painted houses and an artistic, bohemian atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Börek and tea at a local Edirnekapı pastane — under 50 TRY
meals.lunch: Local workers' lokanta near the city walls — full meal under 80 TRY
meals.dinner: Trendy but affordable café dinner in Balat — mezes and wine/raki — under 150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church is one of Istanbul's most underrated gems — far fewer crowds than Hagia Sophia with equally stunning Byzantine art. Balat is extremely photogenic with its colorful staircase streets — very popular on social media but still retains local charm.

day_by_day.morning: Experience a traditional Turkish hammam (bath) — a must-do cultural experience. Visit the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584) or the more budget-friendly Cağaloğlu Hamamı. Basic bath package runs 400-600 TRY including scrub and foam massage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Refreshed after the hammam, explore the Cağaloğlu and Sirkeci neighborhoods. Visit the historic Sirkeci Train Station — the legendary terminus of the Orient Express. Browse the small railway museum inside (free).
day_by_day.evening: Evening visit to the Istanbul Modern Art Museum in Karaköy (entry ~200 TRY) or simply explore Karaköy's art galleries, many of which are free. End the evening with a rooftop bar drink overlooking the Golden Horn.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast spread at a neighborhood kahvaltı spot — under 100 TRY
meals.lunch: Tantuni (spiced meat wrap) from a street food spot near the hammam — under 60 TRY
meals.dinner: Meze spread at a Karaköy meyhane — try sigara böreği, haydari, and patlıcan salatası — under 150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam in advance if possible, especially for weekends. The hammam experience typically takes 1.5-2 hours. Tip the attendant (kese ustası) about 50-100 TRY for a good scrub. Bring flip-flops and keep valuables secured in the locker.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a car-free archipelago in the Sea of Marmara. Ferry from Kabataş (İstanbulkart fare, ~30-40 TRY each way). Visit Büyükada, the largest island, and rent a bicycle (~100 TRY/day) to explore its Victorian mansions and pine forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cycling around Büyükada. Visit the hilltop Aya Yorgi Church for panoramic sea views. Relax on a small beach or in a seaside café. The island has a wonderfully peaceful atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul as the sun sets over the city skyline — one of Istanbul's most beautiful views. Arrive back by 8-9 PM.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast before the ferry — simit and tea at Kabataş pier — under 30 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at a Büyükada waterfront restaurant — slightly pricier but worth it (~200 TRY) — today's splurge
meals.dinner: Simple, light meal at a neighborhood lokanta near the hotel after the long day — under 100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules carefully — the Princes' Islands ferries run several times daily but can get crowded on weekends. May is an ideal month to visit — pleasant temperatures and fewer crowds than summer. No motorized vehicles on the island (except emergency services) — it's wonderfully peaceful.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu (~150 TRY) — housing the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' painting and excellent Ottoman-era artifacts. Explore the surrounding Pera/Tepebaşı neighborhood with its 19th-century European-style architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the full length of İstiklal Avenue slowly, ducking into the historic arcade passages (pasajlar) like the Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) and Avrupa Pasajı. Visit the old Galatasaray Lisesi (high school) courtyard and the nearby French Street (Fransız Sokağı).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening splurge: visit a rooftop restaurant in Beyoğlu for dinner with panoramic views of the Golden Horn, Bosphorus, and city skyline. This is the best way to end your Istanbul experience.

meals.breakfast: Menemen and fresh bread at a local Beyoğlu kahvaltı spot — under 80 TRY
meals.lunch: Çiçek Pasajı beer hall for a classic Istanbul lunch experience — meze and cold Efes beer — under 150 TRY
meals.dinner: Rooftop restaurant with a view — splurge on your last full evening — budget 250-350 TRY for a memorable meal

day_by_day.notes: The Pera Museum is small but excellent quality — budget 1.5 hours. The arcade passages (pasajlar) of İstiklal are architectural gems often overlooked by tourists rushing along the main street. Look up and look inside every ornate doorway.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite neighborhood or spot for a last cup of çay with a view. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Spice Bazaar area (better prices than the Grand Bazaar for food gifts). Pick up Turkish tea, spices, lokum (Turkish delight), and olive oil soap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Head to the airport via Havaist bus or metro (use remaining İstanbulkart balance). Allow 2-3 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry home memories of Istanbul's extraordinary history, flavors, and hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final full Turkish breakfast — treat yourself to the best one of the trip at a scenic spot — under 120 TRY
meals.lunch: Last döner or balık ekmek from a street vendor before heading to the airport — under 60 TRY
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Return your İstanbulkart at the airport or keep it as a souvenir (small deposit refundable). Pack purchased spices in checked luggage to avoid issues at security. The Havaist bus to the airport runs frequently and costs a fraction of a taxi — allow 45-90 minutes depending on traffic. Istanbul traffic can be severe — always add extra time.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along the nearby waterfront promenade to get your bearings. Explore the immediate neighborhood, visit a local market or corner shop to pick up essentials, and enjoy the sea views to decompress after your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby rooftop bar or seaside café for sunset drinks. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner close to the hotel to ease into Istanbul time.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Light bite at the airport or a quick snack near the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local fish restaurant near the waterfront — try grilled sea bass (levrek) with meze starters. Budget ~300–450 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Jet lag may be a factor. Confirm hotel amenities and ask the concierge for a neighborhood map and restaurant recommendations.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast at the hotel, take a ferry or taxi to the Old City (Sultanahmet). Begin with the iconic Hagia Sophia — arrive early to beat crowds. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring this Byzantine masterpiece turned mosque.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) for a guided self-tour. Then explore the Hippodrome of Constantinople and the Egyptian Obelisk. Afterward, wander through the Arasta Bazaar for a preview of local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Sultanahmet Square at dusk when it's beautifully lit. Enjoy dinner in the Sultanahmet district before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish pide (flatbread pizza) at a lokanta (local eatery) near the Hippodrome — budget ~150–200 TRY
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — famous for köfte (meatballs) and lentil soup. Budget ~200–300 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for mosque visits — shoulders and knees covered. Women should carry a headscarf. Hagia Sophia requires an entry ticket (~200 TRY in 2027 est.).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace — the heart of the Ottoman Empire for centuries. Explore the Harem section (separate ticket), the Imperial Treasury, and the sacred relics pavilion. Allow 2.5–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill to Gülhane Park for a peaceful break. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums — three museums in one complex housing artifacts from across the ancient world, including the Alexander Sarcophagus.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Galata Bridge on foot, watching fishermen cast their lines. Enjoy dinner in the Karaköy neighborhood on the other side.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Simit (sesame bread ring) and ayran from a street vendor in Gülhane Park — budget ~30–50 TRY
meals.dinner: Mezze and grilled meats at a mid-range meyhane (tavern) in Karaköy — budget ~350–500 TRY per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace entry ~500 TRY; Harem ~300 TRY extra. Archaeology Museums ~200 TRY. Purchase combo tickets if available. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets. Spend 2 hours browsing spices, ceramics, textiles, and jewelry. Practice friendly bargaining.
day_by_day.afternoon: A short walk away, visit the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü. Purchase saffron, Turkish tea, lokum (Turkish delight), and dried fruits. Then take a short Bosphorus ferry ride from Eminönü to Üsküdar on the Asian side for a change of perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening in Üsküdar — a more local, less touristy neighborhood. Enjoy tea at a traditional çay bahçesi (tea garden) overlooking the Bosphorus.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from a floating boat stall at Eminönü — iconic Istanbul street food, ~80–120 TRY
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional ocakbaşı (grill restaurant) in Üsküdar — budget ~300–400 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Grand Bazaar is closed Sundays. Keep valuables secure in crowded bazaars. The Bosphorus ferry (vapur) is very affordable (~20–30 TRY) and offers great views.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full Bosphorus cruise — book a 2-hour public ferry tour from Eminönü that passes under the Bosphorus Bridge, past Dolmabahçe Palace, Rumeli Fortress, and up toward the Black Sea entrance. Spectacular views of both European and Asian shores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı (the last stop) and climb up to the ruined Yoros Castle for panoramic views of where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Explore the small fishing village.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Eminönü. Head to Beyoğlu and walk up İstiklal Avenue — Istanbul's vibrant pedestrian boulevard — for evening shopping and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish lunch at one of the seafood restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı village — budget ~250–350 TRY per person
meals.dinner: Dinner at a stylish bistro on or near İstiklal Avenue — try modern Turkish cuisine. Budget ~400–550 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Full Bosphorus cruise tickets ~150–200 TRY (public ferry). Book early morning departure to maximize time at Anadolu Kavağı. Bring a light jacket — it can be breezy on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace on the European Bosphorus shore — a stunning 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace with 285 rooms and 46 halls. Guided tours only; allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a taxi to the Beşiktaş neighborhood. Explore the lively Beşiktaş fish market and the surrounding streets. Visit the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) for Ottoman maritime history.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ortaköy — a charming waterfront neighborhood. Browse the Sunday craft market (if applicable), admire the Ortaköy Mosque framed by the Bosphorus Bridge, and enjoy the lively café scene.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Fresh börek (savory pastry) and soup at a traditional börekçi in Beşiktaş — budget ~100–150 TRY
meals.dinner: Dinner at a waterfront restaurant in Ortaköy — try kumpir (loaded baked potato, a local specialty) as a snack first, then seafood dinner. Budget ~350–500 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace entry ~500 TRY. Separate tickets for Harem section. Palace is closed Mondays and Thursdays — check schedule. Photography restrictions inside.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy the beach or pool, have a long breakfast, and recharge at the halfway point of the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to some of the world's finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes. Then walk along a section of the ancient Theodosian Walls.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — Istanbul's most colorful and historically rich districts with Greek Orthodox, Jewish, and Armenian heritage. Wander the rainbow-painted stairways and antique shops.

meals.breakfast: Extended buffet breakfast at the resort — treat it as brunch
meals.lunch: Skip or have a light snack near the Chora Church
meals.dinner: Dinner at a charming local restaurant in Balat — try home-style Turkish cooking (ev yemeği). Budget ~250–350 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Chora Church entry ~200 TRY. Balat is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The neighborhood has excellent photo opportunities with its colorful architecture.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably the most architecturally perfect Ottoman mosque, designed by the legendary architect Mimar Sinan. Explore the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) including the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and Sinan himself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to the Eminönü waterfront and visit the Rüstem Pasha Mosque — a smaller jewel famous for its extraordinary Iznik tile interior. Then explore the historic Tahtakale district, a fascinating wholesale market area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Beyoğlu. Visit the Galata Tower for panoramic 360° views of Istanbul at sunset (book tickets in advance). Explore the bohemian Galata and Karaköy neighborhoods afterward.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish breakfast spread (kahvaltı) at a café near Süleymaniye — budget ~200–250 TRY (Turkish breakfast is served all day)
meals.dinner: Dinner in Karaköy at a modern Turkish restaurant — try dishes like slow-cooked lamb tandir or stuffed eggplant (İmam bayıldı). Budget ~350–450 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: Galata Tower entry ~400 TRY — book online to skip queues. Sunset views are spectacular. Rüstem Pasha Mosque is easy to miss — look for the entrance staircase above the shops.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a ferry from Kabataş to Büyükada, the largest island. No motorized vehicles allowed — rent a bicycle or take a horse-drawn carriage to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or ride to the hilltop Monastery of Saint George for stunning views over the Sea of Marmara. Explore the Victorian-era mansions and quiet pine forests.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul. Enjoy a quiet evening near the hotel, perhaps with a traditional Turkish bath (hamam) experience at a local neighborhood hamam.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a waterfront restaurant on Büyükada — try fried calamari and grilled fish. Budget ~300–400 TRY per person
meals.dinner: Light dinner at a neighborhood restaurant near the hotel — try mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and gözleme (stuffed flatbread). Budget ~200–300 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: Ferry to Büyükada ~1.5 hours each way (~50 TRY with Istanbulkart). Bicycle rental ~100–150 TRY/day. The island gets crowded on weekends — visit early. Hamam costs ~400–600 TRY for a full experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — an atmospheric underground Byzantine cistern with dramatic lighting and the famous Medusa head columns. Then visit the nearby Binbirdirek Cistern for a less crowded alternative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Istanbul Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (İslam Eserleri Müzesi) in Sultanahmet — housing exceptional carpets, manuscripts, and artifacts. Then relax in the adjacent Sultanahmet Park.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a Whirling Dervishes ceremony (Sema) — a UNESCO-recognized spiritual performance. Several venues in Sultanahmet and Beyoğlu host regular shows.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional lokanta (workers' restaurant) near Sultanahmet — choose from daily specials like stuffed peppers or braised lamb. Budget ~150–200 TRY
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner near the Sema venue — try a rooftop restaurant with Bosphorus views. Budget ~400–500 TRY.

day_by_day.notes: Basilica Cistern entry ~400 TRY. Book Whirling Dervishes tickets in advance (~300–500 TRY). The ceremony lasts about 1 hour and is a deeply moving cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Kadıköy neighborhood on the Asian side — take the ferry from Karaköy. Visit the bustling Kadıköy Market (Tarihi Kadıköy Çarşısı) — one of Istanbul's best food markets with fresh produce, cheeses, olives, and spices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the streets of Moda — Kadıköy's trendy, artsy sub-district with independent bookshops, vintage stores, and charming cafés. Visit the Moda coastline park for sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Stay on the Asian side for dinner in Kadıköy's lively bar and restaurant street (Kadife Sokak, known as 'Bar Street'). Experience Istanbul's local nightlife scene.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Food market grazing in Kadıköy — sample kokoreç (offal sandwich), midye dolma (stuffed mussels), and fresh cheese. Budget ~100–150 TRY
meals.dinner: Dinner at a meyhane in Kadıköy with live fasıl music — try cold and hot meze platters with rakı. Budget ~400–600 TRY per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kadıköy is a favorite among locals and gives an authentic, non-touristy Istanbul experience. The ferry ride (~20 TRY) offers great Bosphorus views. Kadife Sokak is very lively after 20:00.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu — housing an impressive collection of Orientalist paintings, Anatolian weights and measures, and the famous 'Tortoise Trainer' painting. Then explore the historic Pera/Beyoğlu district architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (recently relocated to a stunning new waterfront building in Karaköy) — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum with rotating international exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Final major evening in Istanbul — splurge slightly on a rooftop dinner with Bosphorus views. Watch the city light up at night from above.

meals.breakfast: Buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Istanbul Modern café — great views, quality food. Budget ~300–400 TRY
meals.dinner: Special dinner at a rooftop restaurant in Beyoğlu or Karaköy — try Ottoman-inspired tasting menu or upscale Turkish cuisine. Budget ~600–800 TRY per person (slight splurge for the last full evening).

day_by_day.notes: Pera Museum entry ~200 TRY. Istanbul Modern entry ~300 TRY. Book the rooftop dinner reservation in advance — popular spots fill up quickly, especially on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely last Turkish breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping (good options: Turkish tea sets, hand-painted ceramics, evil eye (nazar) amulets, saffron, lokum).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure time, revisit a favorite spot or simply relax by the hotel beach/pool. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and transfer to Istanbul Airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast — simit, white cheese, olives, tomatoes, eggs, and çay (tea) at a local café. Budget ~150–200 TRY
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or at the airport — try a final börek or a Turkish sandwich
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for Istanbul Airport check-in and security. The airport is large — factor in extra time. Keep some Turkish Lira for last-minute purchases or tips. Consider purchasing a bottle of Turkish wine or rakı at duty-free as a memento.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Settle into your suite and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: After freshening up, take a leisurely stroll along the Bosphorus waterfront promenade near the resort. Explore the immediate beachfront neighborhood, soak in the sea breeze, and get oriented with the surroundings. Visit a nearby local artisan bazaar for a gentle introduction to Istanbul's vibrant craft culture.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the resort's rooftop terrace bar overlooking the Bosphorus. Dine at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant for a curated welcome dinner featuring Ottoman-inspired cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or post-arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the resort upon check-in — mezze platters, fresh-baked bread, seasonal fruits, and Turkish tea
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's signature restaurant — multi-course Ottoman tasting menu with dishes such as lamb tandir, stuffed vine leaves, and baklava soufflé, paired with Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH lands at 13:00. Allow approximately 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage, and private transfer. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Confirm private transfer booking in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — one of the world's greatest architectural masterpieces. Your expert guide will walk you through its 1,500-year history, from Byzantine cathedral to Ottoman mosque. Arrive early to beat crowds and enjoy a serene, in-depth experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) and the ancient Hippodrome of Constantinople, including the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column. Continue to the Basilica Cistern for a dramatic underground experience among illuminated ancient columns.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Sultanahmet district at dusk as the minarets light up. Enjoy a private rooftop dinner at a premium Sultanahmet restaurant with panoramic views of Hagia Sophia and the Sea of Marmara.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Turkish breakfast buffet at the resort — white cheese, olives, honey, clotted cream (kaymak), fresh tomatoes, cucumbers, simit, and eggs prepared to order
meals.lunch: Lunch at Matbah Restaurant near Sultanahmet — Ottoman palace cuisine featuring dishes like hünkar beğendi (sultan's delight) and stuffed pigeon
meals.dinner: Dinner at Seasons Restaurant (Four Seasons Sultanahmet) — contemporary Turkish cuisine with Bosphorus views, featuring sea bass with mastic sauce and pistachio-crusted lamb

day_by_day.notes: Book Hagia Sophia private guide in advance. Dress modestly for mosque visits — bring a scarf and remove shoes. The Basilica Cistern may be cool and damp; bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Topkapi Palace — the opulent heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Explore the Harem quarters, the Imperial Treasury (home to the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), and the sacred relics in the Pavilion of the Holy Mantle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums complex adjacent to Topkapi, housing one of the world's finest collections of ancient artifacts including the Alexander Sarcophagus. Afterward, explore the ornate Tiled Kiosk (Çinili Köşk) with its magnificent Iznik tilework.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) for a private after-hours VIP shopping experience arranged through a luxury concierge — browse antique jewelry, hand-woven carpets, and rare ceramics without the daytime crowds.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapi Palace grounds — a historic institution serving classic Turkish dishes since 1897, including stuffed artichokes and lamb chops
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mikla Restaurant (Marmara Pera Hotel rooftop) — New Anatolian cuisine by celebrated chef Mehmet Gürs, featuring dishes inspired by Turkey's diverse regional ingredients, with sweeping city and Bosphorus views

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays — confirm the day aligns. Book Mikla well in advance as it is one of Istanbul's most sought-after dining reservations. Private after-hours Grand Bazaar access requires concierge arrangement at least one week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private Bosphorus cruise aboard a chartered luxury yacht. Sail past the iconic Dolmabahçe Palace, Çırağan Palace, the Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisarı), and the two grand suspension bridges. Your guide will narrate the history of each landmark as you glide between two continents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dock near the Ortaköy neighborhood and explore its charming waterfront square, baroque mosque, and artisan stalls. Visit the Çırağan Palace Kempinski for afternoon tea in its stunning Bosphorus-facing terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Bebek — one of Istanbul's most exclusive waterfront neighborhoods. Enjoy a table at a premier fish restaurant with private Bosphorus terrace seating.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served on board the private yacht — cold mezze, grilled seafood, fresh salads, and Turkish desserts prepared by a private chef
meals.dinner: Dinner at Poseidon Restaurant in Bebek — renowned for ultra-fresh Bosphorus seafood, including grilled sea bream, calamari, and octopus carpaccio, with an extensive raki and wine list

day_by_day.notes: Charter the yacht through the resort concierge or a luxury tour operator. Confirm weather forecast for the cruise. Bring sunscreen and a light jacket as it can be breezy on the water. Bebek is approximately 20–25 minutes from Ortaköy by car.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Dolmabahçe Palace — the lavish 19th-century Ottoman imperial residence on the European shore of the Bosphorus. Marvel at the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier (a gift from Queen Victoria), gilded ceilings, and the room where Atatürk passed away in 1938.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beşiktaş neighborhood — visit the Naval Museum (Deniz Müzesi) with its extraordinary collection of imperial caiques and Ottoman maritime history. Wander through the lively local market streets and observe authentic Istanbul daily life.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Whirling Dervishes (Sema) ceremony — a deeply spiritual Sufi ritual recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. Afterward, enjoy a sophisticated dinner in the Nişantaşı district, Istanbul's most upscale fashion and dining quarter.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lüks Beşiktaş — a contemporary Turkish bistro serving elevated versions of classic Anatolian dishes including mantı (Turkish dumplings) and mercimek çorbası (lentil soup)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nişantaşı's Nicole Restaurant — a Michelin-recognized establishment offering modern Turkish haute cuisine with seasonal tasting menus and an exceptional natural wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires separate tickets for the Selamlık and Harem sections — book in advance. Photography is restricted in some areas. The Whirling Dervishes ceremony venue varies; confirm with the concierge for the most authentic and intimate setting.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a private boat to Büyükada, the largest of the nine islands in the Sea of Marmara. Explore the island by horse-drawn carriage (the only transport allowed) past Victorian-era wooden mansions, pine forests, and Greek Orthodox monasteries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Aya Yorgi Monastery atop Büyükada's highest hill for panoramic sea views. Relax on the island's quiet beaches or explore the charming main square with its boutique shops and cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private boat at sunset. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort with a private in-suite hammam treatment and room service dinner.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Merit Halki Palace Restaurant on Heybeliada (neighboring island) or at a premium seafood restaurant on Büyükada's waterfront — fresh grilled fish, stuffed mussels, and island salads
meals.dinner: Private in-suite dinner at the resort — curated five-course menu delivered by the resort's butler service, featuring meze, slow-cooked lamb, and kunefe for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The Princes' Islands are car-free and peaceful — ideal for a relaxed mid-trip day. Private boat charter is recommended over public ferry for a premium experience. Book the hammam treatment at the resort spa in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) and the surrounding Eminönü district. Learn about the history of the spice trade in the Ottoman Empire, sample exotic spices, Turkish delight, and dried fruits with your expert guide. Visit a master spice merchant for a curated selection to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Golden Horn to explore the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — Istanbul's most colorful and historically layered districts, home to Greek, Jewish, and Armenian communities for centuries. Visit the Ecumenical Patriarchate, the Bulgarian Iron Church, and admire the rainbow-colored historic townhouses.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in the Galata district — explore the area around the iconic Galata Tower and dine at a rooftop restaurant with tower views.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional lokanta (Turkish tavern) in Balat — home-cooked dishes including stuffed peppers, slow-braised beans, and fresh bread from a wood-fired oven
meals.dinner: Dinner at Galata's Gram Restaurant — a celebrated farm-to-table Istanbul restaurant with a focus on Anatolian ingredients and a creative seasonal menu

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for Fener and Balat — the streets are cobblestoned and hilly. The neighborhood is photogenic and vibrant; allow extra time for photography. Balat is undergoing gentrification but retains its authentic charm.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably the most magnificent of all Ottoman mosques, designed by master architect Mimar Sinan in the 16th century. Explore the mosque's complex including its courtyard, tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) in the Edirnekapı neighborhood — home to some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, depicting the life of Christ and the Virgin Mary in extraordinary detail.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private classical Turkish music concert (fasıl or classical Ottoman court music) at a historic venue. Follow with a late dinner at a meyhane (traditional Turkish tavern) in Beyoğlu.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Darüzziyafe Restaurant — housed in the original soup kitchen of the Süleymaniye Mosque complex, serving classic Ottoman recipes in a historic setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refik Restaurant in Asmalımescit, Beyoğlu — a legendary meyhane serving traditional Istanbul mezes, grilled fish, and raki in a convivial atmosphere beloved by locals and connoisseurs alike

day_by_day.notes: The Chora Church may have restricted access depending on ongoing restoration works — confirm with the concierge before visiting. The fasıl concert experience is best arranged through a cultural concierge for an intimate, high-quality performance.

day_by_day.morning: Private cooking class with a renowned Istanbul chef — learn to prepare classic Turkish dishes from scratch, including börek (layered pastry), imam bayıldı (stuffed eggplant), and Turkish coffee. The class takes place in a premium culinary studio in the Karaköy district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Karaköy and Galata neighborhoods — visit the Galata Tower for panoramic city views, browse the contemporary art galleries and design boutiques, and discover the area's rich Genoese and Levantine heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Bosphorus dinner cruise aboard a private luxury vessel — enjoy a curated multi-course dinner as you sail past illuminated palaces and mosques reflecting on the water.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Dishes prepared during the cooking class enjoyed together with the chef and fellow participants — a hands-on culinary feast
meals.dinner: Private Bosphorus dinner cruise — five-course Turkish tasting menu with live classical music, raki, and premium Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least one week in advance. Specify any dietary restrictions when booking. The private dinner cruise should be arranged through the resort concierge — sunset departure (around 19:30 in May) is recommended for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Edirne — the former Ottoman capital, approximately 2.5 hours from Istanbul by private car. Visit the Selimiye Mosque, Mimar Sinan's acknowledged masterpiece and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with its breathtaking central dome and four slender minarets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Edirne's Old Bazaar (Alipaşa and Bedesten Bazaars), the historic Kırkpınar oil wrestling arena, and the beautifully restored Rüstem Pasha Caravanserai. Sample Edirne's famous liver dish (ciğer) and local sweets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private car. Enjoy a quiet, relaxed evening at the resort with a spa treatment and light dinner.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Lalapaşa Restaurant in Edirne — a respected local establishment serving Edirne specialties including fried liver, grilled lamb, and regional mezze
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort's all-day dining terrace — Turkish soup, grilled vegetables, and seasonal desserts

day_by_day.notes: Edirne day trip requires an early start (depart by 08:00). Arrange a private car and driver through the resort. Carry your passport as Edirne is near the Greek and Bulgarian borders. The Selimiye Mosque is a must-see — allocate at least 90 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu — home to the iconic Orientalist painting 'The Tortoise Trainer' by Osman Hamdi Bey, as well as Anatolian weights and measures, Kütahya tiles, and rotating international exhibitions. Enjoy a curator-led private tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the İstiklal Avenue (Istiklal Caddesi) and the vibrant Cihangir neighborhood — browse independent bookshops, antique dealers, and design studios. Visit the historic Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) and the Balık Pazarı (Fish Market).
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at a premier Beyoğlu bar with Golden Horn views, followed by a premium dinner at one of Istanbul's celebrated contemporary restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pera Museum's Müzedechanga café — a stylish bistro serving modern Turkish-Mediterranean cuisine in a chic art museum setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Neolokal Restaurant (SALT Galata) — a Michelin-recognized restaurant by chef Maksut Aşkar, celebrating forgotten Anatolian ingredients and techniques in a stunning historic bank building

day_by_day.notes: Book the Pera Museum private curator tour in advance. Neolokal is one of Istanbul's most critically acclaimed restaurants — reserve well ahead. İstiklal Avenue is pedestrianized and best explored on foot.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury hammam experience at the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı or Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı — one of Istanbul's most celebrated 16th-century bathhouses. Enjoy a full traditional scrub (kese), foam massage, and oil massage in a beautifully restored Ottoman setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) in Sultanahmet — housing an extraordinary collection of Islamic manuscripts, carpets, ceramics, and ethnographic artifacts in a restored Ottoman palace. Private guided tour included.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Istanbul's most prestigious restaurant — a celebratory final evening with a grand tasting menu, exceptional wine pairing, and live traditional music.

meals.breakfast: Grand Turkish breakfast at the resort — the full spread with every regional specialty
meals.lunch: Lunch at Balıkçı Sabahattin in Sultanahmet — an institution since 1927, serving impeccably fresh seafood in a traditional wooden Ottoman house with a garden terrace
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Tuğra Restaurant (Çırağan Palace Kempinski) — imperial Ottoman cuisine in a breathtaking palace setting on the Bosphorus, featuring a grand tasting menu with dishes from the palace kitchens of Suleiman the Magnificent

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam session in advance — the Hürrem Sultan Hamamı (restored by the Turkish Ministry of Culture) offers a particularly premium experience. Tuğra at Çırağan Palace is one of Istanbul's grandest dining experiences — formal dress code applies. Reserve at least two weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a last leisurely Turkish breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk along the beachfront promenade, collect any last souvenirs from nearby shops, and soak in the final views of the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time: optional visit to a nearby gallery or simply relax at the resort's spa or pool. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport arranged by the resort concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Farewell to Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Final grand Turkish breakfast at the resort — savor every last bite of white cheese, honeycomb, fresh simit, and Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the resort's terrace restaurant — fresh salads, grilled fish, and seasonal Turkish desserts before the transfer to the airport
meals.dinner: In-flight or at the airport lounge

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time and arrange late checkout if needed (subject to availability). Ensure all purchased items — carpets, ceramics, spices, and textiles — are properly packed. Keep receipts for any items requiring customs documentation. Private airport transfer should be booked 24 hours in advance.
